correctness.rationale: From the exact generalized Pitman–Stanley defining inequalities, the Euclidean distance normalizations are 1 for coordinate walls, √i for single-column prefix walls and √(2i) for adjacent-column prefix differences. The i=1 inequalities telescope to 1≥r(2+(m−1)√2). Repeating y_j=r[1+(m−j)√2] in every row meets all inequalities since i≥√i, proving the sharp radius for all n≥1,m≥2. Equality fixes all first-row variables. For n≥2 the published ε witness makes every remaining independent inequality strict at an affine point with first row fixed; hence exactly m(n−1) free center dimensions. This symbolic proof is general; the 100×49-case script is corroborative only.

value.rationale: The all-ones generalized Pitman–Stanley family is a natural distinguished multichain/flow-polytope realization. The metric theorem finds an n-independent exact inradius while the ambient dimension grows with n, and classifies which coordinates remain rigid versus the full m(n−1)-dimensional incenter set. It is a symbolic, family-wide and motivated geometric invariant, not an arbitrary numerical slice or finite experiment.

final_claim: For every n≥1 and m≥2, the standard-coordinate generalized Pitman–Stanley PS_n^m(1,0) has sharp Euclidean inradius 1/[2+(m−1)√2], its first row fixed at every incenter, and incenter locus dimension m(n−1).
